title: Efficient Top-k Scoring: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Efficient Top-k Scoring: Visual Guide

1. Top-k Not All-k | the four documents matching 'vector database' with their cosine scores and per-document upper bounds, under a k slider and a heap-full / heap-filling toggle | the tf-idf and cosine score from lesson 02 is unchanged; what this lesson adds is a threshold plus an upper bound, and an empty heap prunes nothing

2. TAAT Versus DAAT | a step-by-step trace of the same two posting lists, showing TAAT's growing accumulator against DAAT's size-k min-heap and its rising threshold | TAAT's state is every document touched while DAAT's is bounded by k, and only DAAT finalizes scores in document order, which is what makes a live threshold and all later skipping possible

3. Champion List Size | r dragged from 100 to the full 1,000,000-document posting, with toggles for eliminating a very common term and for an access filter that rejects nine of ten champions | champion lists and term dropping are heuristics that trade recall for cost, so the fallback condition must be explicit and the guarantee labelled — stopping at k results with a threshold of 0.15 while omitted postings could contribute 0.9 is a guess

4. The WAND Pivot | three iterators at documents 10, 14 and 14 with upper bounds 0.4, 0.7 and 0.8, and a draggable threshold that moves the pivot | bounds are accumulated from the front of the docid ordering until the sum exceeds the threshold, so the pivot is the earliest document that could clear the bar, and when no pivot exists the traversal has proved it can stop

5. Essential Or Skippable | one threshold slider driving two views: MaxScore's essential / nonessential split of the same three terms, and Block-Max block bounds on a term whose global maximum is 4.0 | a rising threshold moves terms out of candidate generation permanently, and a single loose per-term maximum permits no skips at all where per-block maxima permit many
